newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel Q1 budget deficit seen at one bln shekels.
newsitem.headline: Israel Q1 budget deficit seen at one bln shekels.

text.p: The Israeli government's domestic deficit this year through March 28 totalled 850 million shekels, the Treasury's accountant-general Shai Talmon told a news conference on Sunday.

Talmon said a news report that the first-quarter deficit would total about one billion shekels "had a basis". He noted that in the last few days of the month the government's spending increases due to tax rebates and interest payments.
He noted that the first-quarter deficit was "substantially less" than in the same period last year but above the government's target.
Last week the Treasury's outgoing director-general David Brodett said the government's forecast for the first quarter deficit was a "few hundred million shekels".

Talmon said that in the first quarter the government absorbed rather than injected money while the central Bank of Israel injected 12 billion shekels by buying foreign currency to support the exchange rate.

Talmon said the government was behind in its revenue target in the first quarter, mainly because of a decline in real estate and value-added tax revenues, which have have been affected by slower economic growth.
Talmon hinted that further budget cuts would be made only if the central bank agreed to reduce interest rates.
When asked by reporters whether he would recommend additional budget cuts, Talmon replied: "If the cuts are accompanied by complementary measures there may be reason to consider the matter."
The Treasury has urged the central bank to lower interest rates to stimulate growth but the central bank said it could not do so unless the government tightened spending.
The 1997 budget already includes cuts and new revenue measures totalling about seven billion shekels in the approximately 197 billion shekel budget.
Finance Minister Dan Meridor has said he would not consider further cuts until after the first quarter.
